newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares close flat, market seen hesitant. [CORRECTED 17:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares close flat, market seen hesitant. [CORRECTED 17:05 GMT]

text.p: Austrian shares closed barely changed on Tuesday, but well of their session lows after taking some strength from advances on leading international bourses in line with the dollar's renewed gains.
Traders said the key ATX index of 21 blue chips remained hemmed into a narrow trading range between 1,290 and 1,310 points for the next few days amid a lack of new incentives.
"More than 1,300 points in the ATX seems rather impossible these days," said one.

The index lost 0.05 percent or 0.70 points to close the day at 1,297.73 points after hitting an intra-day low of 1,288.95 in the morning. Among its constituents, 11 losers outweighed eight gainers, two issues ended the day unchanged.
(Corrects transposed numbers of losers and gainers).
Steel maker Boehler-Uddeholm led the day's decliners, falling 1.55 percent to finish at 945 schillings.
Gainers were led by beer maker Brau-Union, rising 1.38 percent to 737 schillings.
Water treatment company BWT, which is continuously traded but not included in the ATX, advanced to a fresh all-time closing high for the third day.
BWT gained 10 schillings to 1,860, continuing its recent bull run after it broke through key resistance at 1,700 schillings last week.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX contracts for June delivery were up 4.5 points at 1,301 on turnover of 428 contracts.
